sources.note: Nothing for Kepo'. The general orthography section 0.2(b) discusses only vowel symbols, glottal stop and /gh/; the only stress remarks in the book are in the Sumba section (Onvlee's orthography: 'vowel-length and stress have phonemic values.. commonly stressed on the penultimate syllable of the base word'), about Sumbanese, not Kepo'. The one phonological remark touching Kepo' is segmental (1.1.1.a.ii, Rongga): the Rongga flap 'corresponds with Manggarai /s/, Rembong /j/ or /z/ and Kepo' /r/. It is the reflex of AN *d, *D and *j'. Kepo' plant names (c. 400, e.g. 'Palaquium obovatum: Kp kepo';…
